question: To earn a North Carolina motorcycle license, an applicant must pass:
choice_a: Only a written test, with no riding component
choice_b: A knowledge test and an on-cycle skill test
choice_c: Only a road test conducted in a car
explanation: To earn your license, you must pass a knowledge test and an on-cycle skill test.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.42, 'Earning Your License'

question: Knowledge test questions are based on:
choice_b: Vehicle code section numbers, without any context
choice_c: Information, practices, and ideas from the motorcyclists' handbook
explanation: Knowledge test questions are based on information, practices, and ideas from this manual, requiring knowledge of road rules and safe riding practices.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.42, 'Earning Your License'

question: The on-cycle skill test, according to the handbook, may be conducted:
choice_b: Only on a public interstate highway
choice_c: Entirely in a written, paper format
choice_d: In an actual traffic environment or in a controlled, off-street area
explanation: An on-cycle skill test will either be conducted in an actual traffic environment or in a controlled, off-street area.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.42, 'Earning Your License'

question: Among the sample knowledge test questions in the handbook, it is MOST important to flash your brake light when:
choice_b: Your headlight is already switched on
choice_c: You are parked and about to dismount
choice_d: Traffic behind you is completely absent
explanation: The sample knowledge test's answer identifies flashing your brake light before slowing suddenly as most important, consistent with the Brake Light section's guidance.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.42, 'Knowledge Test (Sample Questions)'

question: Among the sample knowledge test questions in the handbook, if a tire goes flat while riding, it is usually best to:
choice_a: Relax on the handlegrips and take no other action
choice_b: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road
choice_c: Shift your weight toward the flat tire
choice_d: Apply both brakes and stop as abruptly as possible
explanation: The sample knowledge test's answer for a flat tire is to brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road, consistent with the Tire Failure section.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.42, 'Knowledge Test (Sample Questions)'

question: In the sample knowledge test's scenario of a car waiting to enter an intersection ahead of you, the best response is to:
choice_a: Make eye contact with the driver and proceed at full speed
choice_b: Maintain speed and lane position without adjustment
choice_c: Reduce speed and be ready to react
choice_d: Maintain speed and move further to the right
explanation: The sample knowledge test's answer for a car waiting to enter the intersection is to reduce speed and be ready to react.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.42, 'Knowledge Test (Sample Questions)'

question: According to the sample knowledge test, to swerve correctly you should:
choice_a: Shift your body weight quickly without touching the handlebars
choice_b: Turn the handlebars sharply by hand
choice_c: Press the handlegrip opposite the direction of the turn
choice_d: Press the handlegrip in the direction of the turn
explanation: The sample knowledge test's answer for swerving correctly is to press the handlegrip in the direction of the turn, consistent with the Swerving section.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.42, 'Knowledge Test (Sample Questions)'

question: On-cycle skill testing is designed to evaluate a rider's ability to, among other things:
choice_b: Recite the vehicle code from memory
choice_c: Change the motorcycle's oil at the roadside
explanation: You may be tested on your ability to accelerate, brake, and turn safely, and to stop, turn, and swerve quickly, among other basic vehicle control and collision-avoidance skills.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.43, 'On-Cycle Skill Test'

question: Examiners administering the on-cycle skill test may score factors such as:
choice_a: The rider's choice of jacket color
choice_b: Selecting safe speeds and choosing the correct path while staying within boundaries
choice_c: The exact make and model of the motorcycle used
choice_d: How many years the rider has held a car license
explanation: Examiners may score factors related to safety such as selecting safe speeds and choosing the correct path and staying within boundaries.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.43, 'On-Cycle Skill Test'

question: The on-cycle skill test is designed to determine a rider's ability to handle:
explanation: Basic vehicle control and collision-avoidance skills are included in on-cycle tests to determine a rider's ability to handle normal and hazardous traffic situations.
source_note: NC DMV Motorcyclists' Handbook (13th Ed., Sept. 2007), p.43, 'On-Cycle Skill Test'
